name: aldo
desc: Morse code learning tool released under GPL
why: A Morse code trainer from the GNU project, a small old-school audio tool with a genuine signal-and-sound angle.

brief.what_it_is: Aldo is a Morse code learning tool for GNU/Linux, released under the GPL. It plays Morse code through your audio output and asks you to identify it, offering four training modes: Classic (random characters), Koch method (characters added progressively), Read from file (Morse generated from a text file you write), and Callsign (random amateur radio callsigns). You type or select what you hear, and the program checks your answers. Input is audio-based training material generated from text, and output is your practice results and audible Morse.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a plain Morse code learning tool. The Savannah summary describes it as a Morse tutor for practising receiving characters and callsigns by ear.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes the training methods but does not explain the audio or scoring internals. The Koch method plays two characters at full speed (20 wpm) and adds one more character each time you identify at least 90 percent of them. Read from file generates Morse from a text file you write.

commands_seen.context: Debian install on unstable, shown on the homepage as run by root (the homepage shows it after a root@somewhere:~# prompt).
Clones the development repository from Savannah.
Builds from git source (bootstrap, configure, make), then runs the built binary at ./src/aldo. The homepage shows this after an aldouser@somewhere:~/aldo$ prompt.

brief.install_notes: Build prerequisites listed on the homepage are gcc 3.x or later and libao. Source tarballs are on the download page, and the latest listed version is aldo-0.7.7, with the signature available. Older releases are on the old web page. Debian packages it, so on Debian unstable you can use apt-get. Building from git needs the bootstrap step before configure. No accounts, hardware, or runtime configuration are mentioned on the pages I read.
brief.standout: It is a small, old-school audio tool with a sound-first approach, and the Koch method is a well-known adaptive learning scheme for Morse. It is packaged in Debian and has a classic Unix build from source.
brief.status: Probably quiet, though the evidence is mixed. Savannah lists Development Status 5 - Production/Stable, the project was registered in February 2003, and it has 2 open bugs out of 9 total. The homepage names aldo-0.7.7 as latest but gives no release date, and I found no last-commit date. The homepage also describes itself as a Savane-hosted project with 3 active members. Treat maintenance as unknown rather than confirmed active.
brief.caveats: Mainly developed for GNU/Linux, and the Savannah page says the project is not part of the GNU Project even though it is GPL licensed (GPL v2 or later). Build requires a C compiler and libao, so there is some build setup. No Windows or macOS instructions appeared on the pages. The homepage also links to GtkMMorse as another option, which is not covered here.

fetch_log: https://www.nongnu.org/aldo/ - worked; homepage text read in full, which contains the methods, download, Debian, and git sections.

https://savannah.nongnu.org/projects/aldo - worked; I built this URL from the Savannah link text on the homepage rather than copying it from a link, and it returned the project summary used for the license, registration date, development status, and bug counts.
